source.title: Generalization in Reinforcement Learning with Selective Noise Injection and Information Bottleneck
source.authors: M. Igl; K. Ciosek; Ying-Zhen Li; Sebastian Tschiatschek; Cheng Zhang; Sam Devlin; Katja Hofmann

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests supervised-learning generalization on a synthetic classification task and reports RL generalization experiments. Its RL results qualify how regularization methods affect the generalization gap, including worse test performance from dropout or batch normalization in a specified Coinrun setup. The results do not test random-label memorization or the versions’ core supervised-learning claims directly.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own test-set performance and train–test gap results relevant to generalization and regularization. Background statements about random-label memorization and cited results are not rows. Figure-only Coinrun values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The synthetic supervised experiment compares dropout with no regularization in a convolutional classifier, measuring held-out loss across training-set sizes and feature conditions. This bears on V6 in a new setting. The RL return and policy-KL results do not test any supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors demonstrate better feature extraction by VIB in a synthetic low-data task and improved RL performance from IBAC combined with SNI. Their explanation that stochastic regularization harms data and gradient quality is partly conjectural; IBAC alone does not prevent Coinrun overfitting.
record.recipe_differences: The supervised experiment uses a synthetic feature classification task, while the main experiments use PPO-based RL on Multiroom and Coinrun. The paper introduces IBAC and SNI rather than reproducing the cited supervised-learning studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Coinrun outcomes depend on regularizer and SNI setting: dropout implementations underperform the baseline combining weight decay and data augmentation; IBAC-SNI with λ = 0.5 performs better than λ = 1. IBAC without weight decay and data augmentation decreases in test performance with longer training. Multiroom SNI slightly reduces performance on one-room layouts but improves it for more complex layouts.

fits_no_version.finding: VIB learns more general features than the other tested approaches in the synthetic low-data and competing-feature experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Information-bottleneck regularization can favor transferable features in synthetic supervised classification.

fits_no_version.finding: IBAC-SNI achieves 43% and 21% success on two- and three-room layouts, compared with below 3% and zero for other fully trained agents.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IBAC-SNI improves learning across procedurally generated Multiroom environments.

fits_no_version.finding: Coinrun dropout variants converge below the weight-decay-plus-augmentation baseline, while IBAC-SNI improves on that baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effect of added regularization on Coinrun test return depends on the regularizer and SNI configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: Deterministic SNI terms reduce policy KL divergence, and the stochastic dropout term has higher divergence than the stochastic IBAC term.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selective noise injection reduces rollout-update policy discrepancy in the tested PPO setting.

fits_no_version.finding: IBAC without weight decay and augmentation exhibits declining test return with longer training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IBAC alone does not prevent Coinrun overfitting.

record.problems: The main Coinrun return and KL results are shown as figures without extractable values in the supplied text. Coinrun comparisons use three random seeds. The supervised feature experiment is synthetic and does not address random labels or the claim versions directly.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out beyond the figure-only measurements retained as figure-only rows. The paper's Figure 2 includes return curves for Multiroom models and Figure 7 training performance on Coinrun, but they are outside the selected test-performance findings; exact values are not stated in text.

untested.parts: Paired random-label and natural-label fitting and held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparisons and tuning conditions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.

The original image-classification regimes, dropout-induced underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation. The supplied figure text does not resolve dropout effects separately by synthetic training-set size or rate.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus matched random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The supervised experiment makes the study relevant to V6; the RL dropout findings do not. Broadly comparable supervised performance warrants a limited qualitative scope verdict, not a claim that dropout universally fails or a statistically established null effect.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels using the same architectures and training recipes.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.

The paper reports dropout test-performance outcomes in Coinrun but only in figures, without a textual result identifying plotted values; the results do not test the specified supervised-classifier regimes or the joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurement and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removal of memorized training examples and resulting test accuracy.

relationships.reason: Section 5.1 describes dropout, weight decay and no regularization as broadly comparable, with VIB the exception; this provides no clear dropout advantage in this setting. This qualitative verdict rests on the text accompanying R1, whose aggregate figure-only values require repair.
relationships.display_finding: The authors described dropout, weight decay and no regularization as broadly comparable. Their results did not establish dropout's effect separately for each data size and feature setting.
